Performers
Vienna Philharmonic (orchestra), Bruno Walter (conductor) Documented

Commons, the surviving concert-programme catalogue and the Library of Congress essay agree on orchestra and conductor.

[1] [3] [4]
Work version
Unknown Unknown

The recording sources identify the complete movement but do not establish the performing edition or any local alterations. The 1912 full score is used as a structural reference, not proof of the parts on the 1938 desks.

[1] [7]
Recorded
1938-01-16 Documented

16 January is the documented public concert date. Pristine gives 15–⁠16 January 1938 for its reissue; the inspected evidence does not establish whether any rehearsal material entered the issued matrices. The Commons embedded “1962” digitising tag is not accepted as a performance or transfer date.

[1] [3] [4] [5]
Place
Großer Musikvereinssaal, Vienna, Austria Documented

The concert-programme catalogue names the hall and city; Commons uses Musikvereinsaal de Vienne.

[1] [3] [4]
Label
Unknown Unknown

Commons names only an unspecified audio CD. HMV made the original 78-rpm issue, but the CD label used for this upload has not been identified.

[1] [5]
Catalogue
Unknown Unknown

The source CD catalogue number is unknown. Pristine documents the historical ten-disc HMV set as DB 8569–⁠8578; that does not identify the carrier transferred for Commons.

[1] [5]
Matrix, take, sides
Unknown Unknown

Pristine lists the original complete-set matrix series 2VH 7027–⁠7046. The inspected DAHR composer listing did not establish a matrix/take match for this digital source; no exhaustive absence is claimed. Specific takes and a verified movement-to-matrix mapping remain unestablished, so the complete-set series is not presented as a side identification for this file.

[1] [5] [6]
Transfer
Unknown Unknown

No engineer for the source CD or Commons transfer is identified. Gaisberg was the original recording producer and Charlie Gregory the recording engineer, not established digital-transfer credits. Andrew Rose’s named 2013 Pristine transfer is a different reissue and is not the source of this Commons upload.

[1] [4] [5]
Transfer date
Unknown Unknown

No transfer date is established. The embedded digitising value 1962 is not corroborated as a transfer date and is not used as one; neither upload nor release dates substitute for it.

[1] [2]
Processing
Commons supplies an Ogg Vorbis file and an MP3 access derivative. Documented

Embedded metadata names Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20100325 (Everywhere). The original 1938 performance was cut on alternating wax-recording machines, but the intervening CD restoration, equalisation, edits and mastering are not identified for this file.

[1] [2]
Composition rights
The underlying composition is out of copyright where the ordinary life-plus-70 term applies. Inferred, not documented

Mahler died in 1911. This is a term calculation for the composition, not worldwide clearance of an unidentified edition or transfer.

[4] [8]
Recording rights
Territorial: Commons applies PD-EU-audio to the sound recording. Documented

The inspected template expressly concerns expired performer and producer rights in the European Union. This package is admitted on that territorial recording-rights basis, not merely the composition’s age. United States status is not established; no worldwide public-domain clearance is asserted.

[1] [9]

Gustav Mahler, Symphony No. 9, III. Rondo-⁠Burleske — Allegro assai. Sehr trotzig; Vienna Philharmonic, Bruno Walter, conductor. Public concert, 16 January 1938, Großer Musikvereinssaal, Vienna. Unidentified audio CD via Wikimedia Commons; recording tagged PD-EU-audio (territorial, not established as US public domain). Rights statement

  1. Wikimedia Commons — Mahler - Symphony N° 9 - III (B. Walter, 1938).ogg — File-description Summary, date, performers, source “Cd audio”, Licensing PD-EU-audio, duration and MP3 transcode. The recording-specific template was inspected separately from generic Public domain metadata.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  2. Wikimedia Commons — embedded recording metadata — Ogg metadata: digitising field 1962 and Xiph.Org libVorbis I 20100325 (Everywhere). These tags do not independently date the performance, CD issue or transfer.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  3. International Gustav Mahler Society — Wiener Philharmoniker 1937/38, fifth subscription concert — Original printed programme V-002-001296: 16 January 1938; Großer Musikvereinssaal, Vienna; Vienna Philharmonic and Bruno Walter; Mahler Ninth and Mozart K. 504.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  4. Erik Ryding — Mahler Symphony No. 9: Bruno Walter, conductor; Vienna Philharmonic Orchestra (1938) — National Recording Registry essay, added 2015, pp. 1–⁠4: premiere, performance date, Gaisberg and Gregory, alternating wax machines, Walter’s later account, and historical context.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  5. Pristine Classical PASC389 — Walter Mahler Symphony No. 9 (1938) — Reissue metadata: 15–⁠16 January 1938; HMV DB 8569–⁠8578; matrices 2VH 7027–⁠7046; Andrew Rose’s separate 2013 transfer. Reproduced Gramophone review gives side allocation. Not a proven source in the Commons transfer chain.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  6. Discography of American Historical Recordings — Gustav Mahler — Composer discography consulted as a matrix-identification lead. The inspected listing did not establish the Walter Ninth’s takes or identify the source CD; it is not cited as proof of absence from DAHR.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  7. Mahler-⁠Online — Symphony No. 9, GMW 50 — Work identity, 1909–⁠10 composition history, Toblach/New York, manuscript stages, 26 June 1912 premiere and first publication.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  8. Directive 2006/116/EC — copyright term — Articles 1(1) and 8: ordinary authorial life-plus-70 term and calculation from the following 1 January. No universal recording clearance is inferred.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
  9. Wikimedia Commons — PD-EU-audio recording-rights template — Template states expiry of performer and producer rights for the sound recording in the EU; documentation distinguishes those rights from copyright in the underlying composition.. Accessed 2026-10-17.
